quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move when a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half of a lane.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to avoid it.
Stop immediately and block its path.
Clear a path for the vehicle to pass.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clear a path for the vehicle to pass.
questions.explanation: Give the emergency vehicle a clear path. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade ahead.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you there is a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: You notice your vehicle has a safety problem. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any safety problem right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: Your right wheels leave the road. What should you do?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the pavement with a small steering adjustment. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Heavy traffic ahead.
Do not enter.
Railroad crossing.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot enter the road or driveway from your direction. Turn around and find another route.

questions.question: How does speeding affect your vision while driving?

options.text: It increases your field of vision.
It decreases your field of vision.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It has no effect on your vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases your field of vision.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. Stay alert for hazards as your speed increases.

questions.question: What does a solid red HAWK signal mean?

options.text: You may proceed with caution.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Stop completely.
There are no pedestrians nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red HAWK signal means you must stop completely. HAWK signals control pedestrian crossings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road meets a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a median or barrier between them.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Let drivers on the road go first.
Force their way into traffic.
Expect other drivers to move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers on the road go first.
questions.explanation: Always yield to drivers already on the public road when entering from a driveway or private road. Merge into traffic safely when you have space.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume that other drivers will change lanes for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: You must yield to drivers already on the highway when entering from an entrance or acceleration ramp. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: This sign shows:

options.text: An intersection.
A road curve.
A right turn.
A lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Trucks and large SUVs have areas near their rear that drivers cannot see in their mirrors.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. On hills with limited visibility, passing is illegal. Always use caution around large vehicles.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Signal for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. Move to the right side and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, clear it first before stopping.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Don't worry about how many tracks you cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop when approaching railroad tracks. A train or other vehicle may be using the rails.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your vehicle?

options.text: Place them on the back seat.
Put them on the floor near the driver's seat.
Secure them so they don't become hazards.
Keep them on a back shelf.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them so they don't become hazards.
questions.explanation: Secure all loose objects before driving. Unsecured items can injure people during sudden stops or crashes. Objects on the floor can roll under pedals and affect your control of the car.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: Use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning if your turn signals don't work.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. Yield to that driver and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the roadway?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass as close to the animal as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the roadway. Slow down to avoid startling it or hitting it.
